results.title: Effectuation - Overview - UVA Darden School of Business
results.content: Effectuation is the unique logic expert entrepreneurs use to build new firms and markets. Sarasvathy discovered effectuation in the late 1990s as a result of in-depth studies of how expert entrepreneurs think, act, and make decisions in the initial stages of new venture creation. As the CEO of an established company, Lebda encourages effectual thinking, including placing small bets on new ideas using the **Affordable Loss Principle**. According to Lebda, effectuation doesn't just apply to running a business but is also a way of living, which includes being open to surprises, or what Sarasvathy calls the **Lemonade Principle**. With this effectual approach, expert entrepreneurs don't need to predict the future. In doing what they can do with their current means, expert entrepreneurs control the downside by investing only what than can afford to lose. Because they believe that in the uncertain domain of entrepreneurship control works better than prediction, expert entrepreneurs prefer to work with factors directly within their control and less with predicted factors outside their control.
